subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@acmehealth.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: ACME Health — discovery recap & next steps

Hi Ravi / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use case: interactive patient triage assistant embedded in ACME's clinician dashboard (short prompts, streaming responses).
- Key constraints: sub-300ms p50 latency for token stream start, deterministic stop sequences for clinical note generation, and strict PII handling.
- Volume: ~120k requests/day peak, average request length ~120 tokens.

Proposed immediate follow-ups (what we committed to):
1) Share initial model fit recommendations and a baseline prompt set (attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv).
2) Run a short model eval on your sample prompts and share benchmark links.
3) Investigate streaming UX: partial output coherence and stop-sequence behavior — capture latency logs (please send any you have; we attached our example capture).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive next Wednesday (10/21) to review eval results and rollout plan.

If that looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and loop in engineering for the streaming investigation.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming items look correct. We attached an export of 500 sample prompts from our sandbox and a few logs; I’m sharing the S3 link here (internal only): s3://acme-prod-sandbox/exports/triaze_prompts_500.ndjson.

A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- For stop sequences we need absolute determinism on clinical note boundaries (no trailing partial sentences).
- We have an internal guideline that final output should not exceed 220 tokens; streaming truncation should prefer safe stop sequences over mid-sentence cuts.

Next steps: please share the baseline eval results and any quick wins we can enact before the technical deep-dive. Also happy to shift the deep-dive earlier if you can do 10/20.

Best,
Ravi

ravi@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@acmehealth.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & quick benchmark links

Ravi —

Appreciate the prompt export link. We ran a quick baseline eval against two candidate model profiles and a streaming configuration. High-level notes below; I’m attaching the full logs (acme_streaming_latency_logs_1014.zip) and a short evaluation report in the Drive link.

Recommended model candidates (based on your latency & quality requirements):
- redwood-rt-1.7b-fp16 (low-latency, good on short-answer precision). Pros: p50 token-start ~180ms on dedicated T4p pool; cons: may hallucinate on longer context unless prompt templates are strict.
- redwood-2.9b-int8 (higher coherence, better on multi-sentence clinical notes). Pros: stronger stop-sequence adherence with our stop-token handling; cons: p50 token-start ~320ms on same pool.

Baseline results (short eval):
- redwood-rt-1.7b-fp16: exact-stop success rate 86%, average final token count 156, 95th percentile latency for stream-first-token 340ms (on shared hosted profile).
- redwood-2.9b-int8: exact-stop success rate 93%, average final token count 168, 95th percentile latency 420ms (hosted).

Streaming UX quick wins we suggest to reduce partial output/coherence issues:
1) Enforce explicit stop sequences in prompt templates (e.g., "\n\n### END_NOTE\n"), and post-process on the client to prefer stop-token boundary truncation over max_tokens cutting.
2) Reduce temperature to 0.0\u20130.2 for clinical-note generation to improve determinism.
3) Use prefix caching for repeated patient-context tokens to reduce token-start latency.
4) For strict latency SLOs, consider redwood-rt-1.7b-fp16 on Dedicated with an autoscaled pool (we can model cost).

I’ve linked the evaluation artifacts here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-evals
And our internal short eval report: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Eval-report-acme-1014

Next steps I propose:
- Team reviews artifacts and we schedule a technical deep-dive on 2026-10-20 10:00am PT (I’ll send a calendar invite).
- Jordan / Sean to review logs and advise on whether we need model variant fallback rules for peak traffic.

If you want us to prioritize stop-sequence enforcement changes, say the word and we’ll assemble a small config PR for your team to test in sandbox.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Attachments: acme_streaming_latency_logs_1014.zip

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: streaming logs & fallback suggestions

Team —

Quick internal notes after looking at the logs Marissa attached: 
- The partial output/coherence incidents correlate with sessions where the client-side stop sequence was missing or malformed; in several traces the model emitted punctuation that met our stop heuristics later than expected.
- The p50 vs p95 divergence suggests occasional cold KV-cache misses — recommend prefix caching for patient context for at least the first 3 requests in a user session.
- For deterministic clinical boundaries, we should add a server-side finalizer that trims to the last complete sentence if a stop-token wasn't observed but max_tokens is reached. This avoids mid-sentence truncation.

Action items: 
- Sean: can you estimate engineering effort for server-side finalizer + configurable stop-token enforcement?
- Marissa: confirm if ACME wants us to push a sandbox config this week for their QA team.

-Jordan
Principal Solutions Architect

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ravi Singh <ravi@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Health — model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Ravi / Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks — we can deliver a sandbox config this week. Short note on engineering ETA: server-side finalizer + configurable stop-token enforcement is ~3 engineer-days to implement and 1 day QA. We can also expose a "hard_stop=true" flag in the streaming API for your sandbox so your QA can validate deterministic boundaries.

Marissa: scheduling the 10/20 deep-dive works. I’ll attach a minimal sample config in the sandbox once I push.

Ravi: will you confirm whether your QA team prefers: (A) stop-token + finalizer, or (B) strict length enforcement to 220 tokens with client-side post-process? Our recommendation: (A) for safety and clinical correctness.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
